transcript.text: How is everybody doing? Welcome back to another Dragon Wild video. I've been covering Dragon Wild since day one of
early access. And after hundreds of hours playing, I picked up a lot of things that can make your play through
much smoother. So whether you're coming back for 1.0 or jumping into Ashenfall for the first time, here are 50 plus
essential tips to help you get started, progress faster, and learn a few things you may have missed. These first ones
are pretty basic, but when you first enter Ashenfall, speak to the wise old man in the church and follow the main
quest for a little bit. It introduces you to early systems, gives you important unlocks, and naturally points
you towards where you should be progressing. Now, with this being a survival game, your three main survival
meters are hunger, thirst, and rest, and each one affects your character differently. Letting your hunger
completely drain will eventually start costing you health, but you will not die. It will stop at one. Keeping thirst
filled helps your stamina regeneration over time, and rest will drop gradually as you stay awake. If it gets too low,
it starts reducing things like your maximum stamina, how much hunger and thirst you can hold, as well as your
stamina regeneration and recovery, overall making everything harder to maintain. So, sleeping or resting at
your base restores this. Now, one of the biggest parts of progression in Dragon Wilds is your power level. Your power
level is a way of showing how prepared your character is for the difficulty of the content you're fighting. Your
displayed power level is based on the armor you currently have equipped. Keep in mind, if you do mix different tiers
of gear, the game averages them together and rounds them down. Now, in Dragon Wands, you'll be pushing into regions
one tier above your power level, but if enemies are significantly higher than you, the difficulty increases quickly,
and you'll start seeing skull indicators beside their health bars. Now, one of the basic fundamentals in Dragon Wilds
are runes. Runes are used for far much more than just combat magic. You'll need them for skill spells, movement,
gathering, utility, and eventually load stone fast travel. So, start building up a supply very early on. Whenever you
find rune essence, be sure to grab it right away. You can also find a Neem event vents around Ashenfall that
produce specific rune types. One especially very useful early location is the law rune vent near the starting
church because law runes become extremely important later on in your progression. Now, when you collect rune
essence for the first time, this will unlock a crafting station called the rune alter. This crafting station is
used to craft runes, which are the resource required to cast all your spells. There are seven different type
of runes in Dragon Wilds. These are used for casting combat magic as well as utilizing your utility spells that you
will eventually unlock. At the starting church, there's one piece of gear that can boost your progression immediately.
What you're going to want to do is go outside onto the right side and climb onto the roof and open the chest to
unlock the wooden training sword recipe. And it's going to be a power level two weapon and only requires ash logs to
craft, making it one of the easiest immediate weapon upgrades you can get. There is another piece of gear that is
very easy and great to obtain early. And this is going to be just northwest up this small hill of the church. Once up
there, there's a chest at the top of the Temple Woods windmill containing the recipe for the leggings of lightness.
They weigh almost nothing and they give you plus 50 maximum carry weight, which is extremely useful, especially early on
when you're constantly gathering resources. Now, Dragons does offer an unstuck feature, and I use this feature
more often than you would think. All you need to do is open up your menu and down here you have to hold X on PC and you
will reposition yourself. What this is going to do is going to send you back to the starting zone at the church. And
once you have load stones active, you can then use this load stone to fast travel to any of the load stones you
have throughout the map. This is very useful and I usually use it if I get stuck somewhere on the map or if I'm
about to fall off the edge of the map or a cliff and die. It's basically a fail safe. Now, dragon loans will constantly
send you back to resources from earlier regions. So don't assume something becomes useless just because you've
moved forward. Wood, ore, plants, hides, ingredients, and other basic materials continue being used throughout your
entire progression as well as your entire time in Ashenfall. So keep that in mind. Early tier ingredients that you
find in the tier one zone will be useful in later regions. One really important resource early on is flax. Flax looks
like a small blue flowering plant and is one resource I would never ignore. It can be turned into coarse thread, which
is used throughout crafting and gear progression, including later tiers. Start stockpiling it long before you
think you need it. Next off, water is used constantly for survival, cooking, farming, and recipes. Early on, I
recommend collecting a large amount of water at once. Roughly two full stacks of 99 is a good starting supply. Build a
campfire, put it into the campfire to process it into clean water, and then let it run while you're doing other
things. Now, sometimes you're going to be coming across chests, and these are scattered all throughout Ashenfall and
can give you regional resources, recipes, buildable items, equipment, and vestages. Remember where chests are
because they will respawn after a few in-game days, and they can be farmed over and over, and everything that's
inside of it is all RNG based, so keep that in mind. Now, I mentioned vests. What are vests? Vestages are some of the
major gear chase items in Dragon Wilds. Studying them unlocks recipes for special weapons, armor, and other
equipment. Some come from chests, packs the enemies drop, quests, or specific locations. Now, their drop is RNG based,
and every region has its own collection of vests. And be sure to study every vest message you find. And keep in mind,
there probably is plenty of vestages you have not found in every region. So, farm
these up to be sure you've collected all gear pieces and special recipes for each region. Now, on top of this, chests,
anemma events, rune geysers, plants, ore deposits, and many other resources in Dragon Wilds will replenish after a few
in-game days. If you find a valuable farming location or an ore that you want to collect a lot of, remember its
location and you can return to it later and repeatedly gather from the same area. Another area that you want to
check very frequently is going to be your journal. It's going to have entries on every single thing you have
encountered in the world. things like fauna, flora, different characters, lore scraps, as well as different recipes
that you have crafted. If you're struggling to figure out how to craft a specific item, be sure to check your
journal and it'll show you the required materials in order to craft that item, as well as what crafting station you can
craft the item at. Check your journal very frequently because it'll have plenty of updated journal entries to
give you a better understanding on every single thing that you discover about Dragon Wilds. Because resources, plants,
and chests respawn, get into the habit of marking important locations. Open your map with M and rightclick where you
want to place a permanent marker. I use these for rare resources, vaults, bosses, useful and neem events, hidden
locations, and anything I want to revisit later. You can also middleclick the map to place a temporary waypoint
that will shoot up into the sky for you to follow. Now, while you're going through Ashenfall, you're going to be
collecting a plethora of different resources and ingredients. If you find an item and have no idea what it does,
be sure you keep it for now. Dragon Wilds has materials tied to later quests, crafting recipes, gear upgrades,
and other systems. It's usually easier to store something that you don't think you need now than to discover hours
later that you need the item you didn't pick up or threw away. Now, one of the biggest progression loops in Dragon
Wilds is the recipe system. We've already gone over this quite a bit, but recipes unlock in several different
ways. Some come from skill levels. So, as you're leveling each skill, you will eventually unlock new recipes for new
craftables. Other ways are from vestages or quests. But another important method
that a lot of people miss is discovering new materials and bringing them back to the correct crafting station. Whenever
you find a new ore, wood, hide, or other useful material. Upon picking it up, you will unlock a few recipes, but be sure
to bring it back to your base with it in your inventory and open up the menu for
different crafting stations because this can trigger entirely new crafting options. Now, with this being a survival
crafting title, your base is going to be your main hub for every single thing you do in the game. Now, your first base
doesn't need to be perfect. It doesn't need to be big. I don't recommend building it too big. What you want to do
is look for a relatively flat ground with easy access to trees, stone, and especially water nearby. Water becomes
increasingly useful for drinking, cooking, farming, and plenty of different crafting recipes. Don't spend
your first few hours building a massive base. Now, guys, I love building in these titles. You can build as big as
you want, but to start, keep it very simple and keep everything compact and focus on what you actually need.
Storage, a bed, cooking stations, the crafting stations you unlock, as well as space for future expansion. Keep in
mind, you are going to expand once your progression gives you a reason to. Now, when you place your first foundations to
start building your base, I recommend a bed being one of the first things you place. Interacting with a bed will link
that bed as your spawn point in the world. So, if you die anywhere out in the world, you have a safe location to
return to, and you have the ability to spawn back at your base. Now, while at your base, you'll notice a coziness perk
at the bottom left of your screen. This is tied to your claimed bed. When you're
near your bed, your survival meters like sustenance, thirst, and rest drain much more slowly. This gives you plenty of
time to build, organize your base, craft new equipment, and prepare for your next trip without constantly worrying about
your meters dropping. When you do leave your base, the coziness perk will remain active for an extra four minutes,
allowing you a buffer when you start your next adventure. One of the biggest things with bases, especially in
survival crafting titles and dragon wilds, is your storage systems. I recommend placing chests as soon as you
start building your first base. This is going to assist you when you're bringing
plenty of resources home and you want to offload them. Be sure every time you build a chest, you're taking advantage
of the linked storage system. This is an option in the chest UI. Make sure it's checked off cuz this will allow crafting
and building to pull resources directly from link chest. You don't constantly have to move every material into your
inventory first. And keep in mind chests do have a radius. So if they're too far away from a specific crafting station,
you will not be able to pull the materials from that. There will be a little bit of a sparkly indication when
you place a chest indicating what crafting stations it is currently linked to. Now, this is very simple, but when
it comes to storage, I recommend you organizing it before it gets out of control. Separate your resources early
on because there are a ton of things you're going to be gathering in Dragon Wilds. I normally use simple
categorizations like wood, ore, and stone, food and ingredients, farming supplies if you're going to start a
farm, any gear pieces, as well as raw materials. Once you're gathering resources from multiple regions,
organized storage saves a huge amount of time, especially later on in the title. So, start your organization early, and
you're going to thank yourself later on. The next major thing I recommend you doing is set up a basic cooking area.
This will allow clean water and other supplies to be processed while you're out exploring. This gives you useful
resources in the background and is also one of the easiest ways to start building cooking XP naturally. Just like
bringing resources to certain crafting stations, any ingredient that you cook or process in Dragon Wilds is going to
unlock a plethora of new recipes that include that certain resource. So, if you have meat, you're going to have
recipes for the raw version of it, as well as for the processed cooked version. So, everything you have, if it
has the ability to cook, I recommend you just dumping it into a campfire and letting it just passively cook while you
go out in the world and explore. Keep in mind, your base can get occasionally targeted by a raid. This will trigger a
group of enemies to spawn nearby and target you at your base. And raid difficulty is influenced by the region
where your base is built. And bases in earlier areas generally deal with easier raids, while bases in higher tier
regions can attract stronger enemies as well as more enemies at a time. Now, for a new player, and honestly, through my
hundreds and hundreds of hours all the way through early access, I recommend keeping your main base in one of the
safer starting areas. My main base throughout the entire early access has been in Bramblemead Valley and that is
where I just set up shop and I've kept it there because the raids are very infrequent there as well as their
difficulty scaling is very low. Now keep in mind raid enemies will target you not your building but the raid enemies can
absolutely obliterate your base extremely fast. So when they come, I recommend you running a little bit away
from your base and kiting them away because there has been many times where I have been in a room at my base and the
enemies go to target me, but they start breaking foundations which break my chest, which break my crafting stations,
and it just makes a complete mess that I have to pick up. So when a raid comes, try to run to the side of your base or
away from any structures to the enemy attacks that are meant for you. Do not accidentally break some of your
structures. Now, this is a small and simple tip, but I recommend keeping a recovery kit at home. Keep some backup
food, extra armor if you have the ability to craft it, as well as weapons and tools. If you die somewhere
dangerous or far away from your base, you don't want all of your useful equipment sitting inside your gravestone
while you have nothing available to recover with it. On normal difficulty, you can have up to 10 active
gravestones, so you usually don't need to panic and immediately run back to gather your equipment. I recommend you
re-equipping gear, grabbing supplies, and preparing first before you go out to your gravestone. Next off, I recommend
you keeping the three main tool types with you whenever you're out exploring. They will take up some of your weight
and inventory space, but there's buried chests throughout the world. Hidden areas, quests, environmental
interactions, trees, and ore deposits can all require specific tools. And in my opinion, I carry all three tool types
with me at all times because I'd rather have the tool ready when discovering something new than have to return to
that location later. Now, with this being a Runescape style title, skills are the major part of progression for
Dragon Wilds, and most of them will be leveling up naturally through what you're already doing. Wood cutting
levels from chopping trees, mining from mining, cooking from cooking, construction from building, and combat
skills from the different fighting styles. As skills increase, you unlock recipes, equipment, passive bonuses,
abilities, and skill spells that make the rest of the game a lot easier. So, as you're leveling up these skills, I
wouldn't only look at your current skill level. Look at what you're about to unlock for each skill. Sometimes you're
only a few levels away in a specific skill from something extremely useful, like wind step, speeding up your
exploration, or actual projection assisting you in wood cutting. Use these upcoming unlocks to decide what skills
are worth actively leveling. Now, you're going to have plenty of time to be leveling skills up. Like I said, you're
going to be leveling them very naturally through every single thing you do in Dragon Wilds. You don't need to be
grinding your skills out to super high levels. So, just focus on reaching important milestones and useful passive
as well as skill unlocks first. You can always come back and push skills to higher levels later when it is necessary
to do so. Now, agility came really late in early access, and in my opinion, it is one of the most important skills in
the title. Agility gains XP passively from running around on foot, jumping, climbing, whatever you're doing. And as
it levels, you'll unlock movement abilities like windstep, double jumping, as well as air dash. And at later
levels, you're going to have a passive increase to your sprint efficiency, stamina efficiency, and increase to your
maximum carry weight at levels 50 and 75. But keep in mind, simply exploring on foot is already going to help you
level one of the most useful skills in the title. But if you do want to grind any skill, this is a very good skill to
grind very early on. Now, a next skill that is very important in a lot of your progression, your crafting, and your
ability to build certain crafting stations as well as build higher tier bases is construction. Now, you don't
necessarily need to rush construction early, but at level 40 is a milestone I recommend you getting to as fast as
possible. This is going to unlock a spell called personal chest. This gives you access to a personal storage while
you're away from your base and becomes extremely useful for gathering inventory management and longer trips. It's
basically just an additional inventory that doesn't add any weight to your character. I use this personal chest for
very specific resources, which we are going to go over in a minute here. Don't unlock skill spells and forget about
them. I know that sounds simple, but it can be easily overlooked. Dragon Wilds gives you a ton of abilities for
movement, increasing gathering, farming, combat, storage, and general utility, and some completely change how you're
going to approach and play the game. Be sure to add these useful spells to your spell wheel and get comfortable using
them as part of your normal gameplay. That's one of the biggest things. As you level up, check your spell wheel,
organize it in a very specific way, and apply those skills to your spell wheel because this is one of the biggest
gameplay elements in Dragon Wilds to increase the efficiency of everything that you do. This next category is going
to relate to food, cooking, as well as farming, which is arguably one of the most important skills in the title. Food
is your main source of healing in Dragon Wild. Food will give you direct HP recovery. I like to think of it as part
of my combat loadout rather than something you only eat for your hunger meter. I recommend keeping plenty on you
before entering harder regions, vaults, or boss encounters. And if you're mainly
looking for straightforward HP recovery, fish are especially useful in this regard, especially early on. Other meals
do become more valuable because of the buffs and perks they will provide you. So eventually, I do recommend carrying
both strong healing food as well as meals that support your build. And overall, as you're progressing your
artisian skill, which is cooking, better cooking stations will eventually unlock, which will give you stronger meals,
drinks, and more useful combinations of ingredients. As the game gets harder, cooking becomes increasingly important
for keeping yourself properly supplied, and it is the most important part of your survival in Dragon Wilds.
I recommend starting a small farm very early on at your base because it can provide you with a renewable supply of
ingredients for food, drinks, buffs, and other supplies like potions. Get a few farming plots running early and let the
crops grow while you're out doing other things, exploring, gathering resources because you're going to want to level up
farming because again, it is arguably the most important skill in the title. Now, how do you actually farm? In order
to farm, you're going to have to collect seeds. Seeds come from several sources in Dragon Wild. You can get them while
gathering plants around Ashenfall, opening chests, as well as looting enemy packs. I recommend you start saving them
when you first encounter them, even if you do not have a farm build, as you're eventually going to want to have a
massive supply once you're ready to start planting them. Now, you don't need to grow every crop simply because you
have the seeds for them. Look at the foods and drinks you're constantly making or the ones that you're looking
at crafting and grow the ingredients for those recipes in bulk. The goal is to come home from exploring and already
have another supply waiting for you, so you're always re-upping your food, water, as well as buff supply. Now,
eventually, you will unlock compost. Don't automatically throw away burnt food, weeds, and other usable organic
materials because a lot of that waste can be recycled into compost, which improves your farming setup and helps
you get way more from your crops. Now, these next tips are going to go over exploration vaults as well as the fast
travel system in Dragon Wilds. Now, throughout your time with Dragon Wild, you're going to hear two terms that you
may not understand at first. This is going to be Binmore and Gornfell. All that these terms are are locations on
the map. Binmore is comprised of three sub regions. This being Temple Woods, Bramblemead Valley, and Whispering
Swamp, as well as Gornfell Sub regions, Fractured Plains, Storm Touch Highlands, and Blood Bllight Swamp. I know this
sounds simple, but you're going to read lore scraps. You're going to be doing quests, and you're going to be finding
things out in the open world, and they will not necessarily refer to those map locations like Stormtouch Highlands or
Whispering Swamp. They may refer to them as Gornfell or Binmore. So, just keep that in mind while you're exploring.
Vaults are arguably some of the most important locations you'll find while exploring Ashen Fault. They can contain
special loot you can't find elsewhere in the game, recipes, vestages, vault cores, and other progression materials.
Their difficulty increases with the region you find them in. If a vault feels too difficult, mark it on your map
and come back once your power level improves or you have the right food with the right buffs. Now, vaults are not a
oneanddone location. Resources inside them, including vault cores, enemies, and chests, will replenish after a few
in-game days. Once you find a vault that seems easy for you to farm, it will become a reliable location to farm
repeatedly. I recommend you collecting as many vault cores as you possibly can. And the reason for that is a buildable
called a load stone. Load stones in Dragon Wilds is the fast travel system. You're going to unlock the recipe for
the first time after you collect your first vault core. And from there, you can build load stones all throughout
Ashenfall, and it'll give you the ability to travel between the ones you've placed. This is another reason
your first vault is an important progression milestone. But when you get to a vault, I recommend you doing it as
soon as possible so you do have the ability to get as many vault cores as well as start building your load stone
system. Now, keep in mind load stones cost law runes and that's why I went over the anemma event at the beginning
of the video by the church that's very easy to farm early on. The cost to use load stones is affected by how far
you're traveling and how much weight you're currently carrying in your inventory. Longer trips with a heavier
inventory is going to cost you more law runes. That's why farming law runes early and placing load stones
intelligently can save you a lot of resources later. I cannot stress it enough. Law runes are going to be one of
the biggest resources and one of the most important runes that you're going to want to farm and have a plethora of.
It is very easy to burn through law runes in the game, but they are also not hard to craft as well as collect. Now,
another interesting POI that was added later on in early access is called constitution shrines. These are going to
provide you with a permanent increase to your maximum HP. Whenever you find one, I recommend you activating it
immediately. They're going to appear on your map as an icon that looks like this. So, if you're nearby it, I
recommend you going to it because these health upgrades are going to stack up over time and become increasingly
important as you move into harder regions. Now, at this point, you're probably progressing through the main
quest. But don't simply run from one quest marker to another. Explore the areas you're already being sent through
because that's where you're going to find chests, resources, vestages, constitution shrines, vaults, hidden
locations, and other useful NPCs which will give you side quests. Now, side quests are another part of progression.
They can unlock things like mounts, equipment, recipes, tools, new systems, overall decoration items, and other
useful rewards. Whenever you reach a new region, talk to the NPCs you find and see what they have available for you in
terms of quests. And some of these quests tie directly into the main story line for that region. Keep in mind side
quests are very important to do before you move on to the next region. They're not 100% necessary, but they're going to
give you plenty of useful resources as well as special vestage drops. Now, our next set of tips are going to go over
gear and gathering. Keep in mind your gathering tools like the pickaxe, your logging axe, as well as your shovel, all
have their own power levels. As you move into higher tier regions, you'll find resources that require stronger
pickaxes, logging axes, and other tools. I recommend you upgrading them immediately when you reach a new region
tier. So, don't focus on upgrading your gear yet. When you go to a new region, you're going to want to upgrade your
tools as your first priority because higher level tools are also going to make gathering faster, and it's going to
give you the ability to gather the resources you need a lot faster in order to get a full new gear set for that
tier. When you are farming or deposits, they can also give you gems. And I recommend saving every single gem you
find. Different regions and ore types can give you different gems. And mining perks like gem prospector, which you
will eventually unlock as you level mining, can improve your chances of finding these gems. Gems feed directly
into jewelry crafting is where you'll craft rings and amulets. They will provide you with powerful bonuses for
gathering, skill, XP, combat, and general utility. When you enter a new region, mining its ores can also help
you unlock the jewelry progression tied to that area. So, if you've gone into a new region and you're mining a new ore
deposit for that area, be sure you mine it until you get new gems to drop because it is RNG based and these gems
are going to help you a lot with your progression for each region. Now, last but not least, we're going to go over
combat and preparation. Combat becomes a lot easier once you learn when to block, parry, dodge, and back away instead of
just simply attacking non-stop. Now, combat isn't super complicated in Dragon Wilds, but those are the few things that
you do want to keep in mind. Managing your stamina is very important when it comes to combat encounters, especially
when you're in boss fights as well as vaults or harder content. If you empty your entire stamina bar by attacking,
you're going to have nothing left when you need to defend yourself, get away, or parry an attack. Now, keep in mind,
don't expect one weapon or damage type to work equally well against every enemy that you encounter in Dragon Wilds.
Different enemies can have different resistance and weaknesses. So melee, range, magic, and different elemental
types for your staff can all perform differently depending on what you're fighting. If an enemy feels unusually
tanky, try changing your weapon, damage type, or combat style to see which combat style does the most damage for
that enemy type. Now, even if you do have a main combat style, I highly recommend you carrying at least one
backup option. A bow or spell lets you pull individual enemies away from groups, attack safely from range, and
switch damage types when your main weapon isn't effective. And having options makes combat a lot easier.
Honestly, like I said, I carry all three tools with me, but I also carry all three weapon types, magic, range, as
well as melee. Part of that is you want to be leveling up these skills together. You don't want to be leveling up one
more than the other. Obviously, sometimes you might be using melee more and it will slowly level more than the
others, but you want to be leveling these up in unison. It's going to make combat easier as you progress into
harder regions. This was just a quick run through of 50 plus starting tips to help you on your journey in Ashenfall. I
have in-depth guides on all skills, regions, as well as quests in Dragon Wilds. So, if you'd like any more
guidance in the game, be sure to check out the channel. And if you enjoyed this video, drop a like on it as it helps me
and the channel grow. And subscribe for all things Dragon Wilds. That's what we do here. We'd love to have you.

comments.text:
A few things:
Vaults are marked on your map with their own icon. You don't need to mark them yourself.
Anima vents are useful but certain types (nature, astral) are less useful. I have thousands of them and only collect more for runecrafting exp. Earth, fore and law are the most important (in my opinion), because using magic to mine will speed things up significantly and law will be needed to teleport.
Chests: pressing F will put things from your inventory to the chest if it already had it. This can speed up putting things away after farming.

Definitely gotta make some notes about hard mode in case viewers are playing hard mode!!

If you die in hard mode, you have to get your gravestone back as you only get ONE gravestone, and dying again without getting the gravestone will make it disappear.

However, AS LONG AS YOU HAVE NOTHING ON YOU (can have equipped gears equipped though) you can KEEP DYING and your gravestone will stay there, but if you have even ONE branch or water or anything and die AGAIN then your gravestone will disappear, in hard mode.
